1.Headline: Adding profiles
1.1: To get started you just need to enter your allycode in the box in the header. The application will then fetch your profile's data and create a new profile for you.
1.2: If you want to add another profile, open the profiles dropdown at the top and select "New Allycode...". Then enter the allycode for that profile and hit enter.
1.3: If you added multiple profiles, you can switch between them by selecting the profile you want to use in the profiles dropdown at the top.
1.4: You can also import profiles from a backup file. When you have at least one profile, you can open the settings. Go to the "Basics" section (default), where you can find the "Backups & Reset" settings. There you can import a backup file that contains one or more profiles. The data will be merged with your existing profiles.

2.Headline: Deleting a profile
2.1: To make mods-manager forget your profile, go to the "Basics" section in the settings and select the profile you want to delete in the "Accounts" widget. It lists all profiles with allycode and in-game name. Then click the "Delete account <allycode>" button. This will remove all data for that profile from mods-manager.
2.2: After deletion of a profile you can always create it again by entering the allycode and fetching the profile's data (mods, characters,...) again, but anything you changed manually like compilations, targets will be lost unless you have a recent backup file that contains the profile.

4.Headline: Fetching your mods as a HotUtils customer
4.1: HotUtils is another tool for SWGoH that, if subscribed to, can directly log in to your game account.
4.2: One of the advantages of this is that it can pull all of your mod data, including unequipped mods.
4.4: HotUtils functionality breaks the terms of service for Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes.
4.5: You assume all risk in using this tool.
4.6: Grandivory's Mods Optimizer is not associated with HotUtils.
4.7: To use HotUtils with mods-manager, it needs your HotUtils Session ID. i put detailed instructions on how to get it on
4.8: After successfully adding your HotUtils Session ID, the fetch button will show a samall flame to indicate it now uses HotUtils

5.Headline: Importing unequipped mods using C-3PO bot
5.1: You can import unequipped mods using the C-3PO bot on Discord. This is slightly more complicated than using HotUtils, but it's also free.
5.2: Use the "/allycode auth ea_connect" command to connect the bot with the game.
5.3: After connecting the bot, you can use the command "/inventory export". The bot will then fetch the mod data and generate a file that you can import into mods-manager.
5.4: You can find the import in the settings under "Basics" (default) in the "Accounts" section. There you can import the file that the C-3PO bot created.

1.Headline: Global optimization settings
1.1: The global settings apply to every character during an optimization. They always override any character-specific settings that you have set.

If this number is above 0, then the optimizer will only recommend that you change mods on a character if the new recommended set is at least this much better than what the character previously had, or if the character's mods were moved to a character higher in your list and needed to be replaced.
1.5: If this box is checked, then no mods will be taken from characters that aren't in your selected list. If you have a number of unassigned mods, this can be a quick way to make use of them without triggering a major remod of your whole roster.
1.7: If this box is checked, the optimizer will try to keep mod sets together, so you always get the maximum set bonuses. Sometimes it's not possible to do so, either because of other restrictions on a character's target or because you don't have enough mods left to make a full set. In these cases, the optimizer will still drop this restriction to try to recommend the best set.

3.Headline: Weights
3.1: The modscore is the weighted sum of all stats of a mod. The weights are defined here. There are two modes: Basic and Advanced.
3.2: Basic: Weights are normalized to fit the range of values for that stat. All weights are between -100 and 100. For example, giving speed and protection the same weight means that 1 speed will score the same as 200 protection (since you find 200x more protection on mods than you do speed).
3.3: Advanced: Now there is no range for the weights and weights are multiplied with the stat directly. If two stats have the same weight one point of the first stat is worth the same as one point of the second stat. If you give speed and protection the same weight, the optimizer will never select speed, because it can more easily give that character much more protection. I suggest sticking to basic mode until you have a strong sense for how the tool works.

1.Headline: Welcome to Grandivory's Mods Optimizer for Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes™!
1.1: This application will allow you to equip the optimum mod set on every character you have by assigning a value to each stat that a mod can confer. You'll give it a list of characters to optimize along with the stats that you're looking for, and it will determine the best mods to equip, one character at a time, until your list is exhausted.
1.2: To get started, enter your ally code in the box in the header.

2.Headline: How does this work?
2.1: Welcome to my mods optimizer for Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes!
2.2: This application works on a simple principle:
2.3: Every stat should have some set value for a character, and if we know all of those values, then we can calculate how much a given mod, or set of mods, is worth for that character. From there, the tool knows how to find the set of mods that give the highest possible overall value for each of your characters without you needing to look through the hundreds of mods in your inventory!

3.Headline: Selecting characters to optimize
3.1: The mods optimizer will start out by considering all mods equipped on any character other than those that are "Locked". Then, it will go down the list of selected characters, one by one, choosing the best mods it can find for each character, based on the selected target. As it finishes each character, it removes those mods from its consideration set.
3.2: Therefore, the character that you want to have your absolute best mods should always be first among your selected characters. Usually, this means that you want the character who needs the most speed to be first.

4.Headline: Picking a target
4.1: Every character in the game has targets. (A collection of predefined weights for all character stats and sometimes mod restrictions). The optimizer will pick the best value mods according to the given weights/restrictions. The targets have been named for their general purpose - 'hSTR Phase 1' or 'PvP' for example. Some characters have multiple different targets that you can select from.
4.2: These targets, while directionally good for characters, are only a base suggestion!
4.3: There are many reasons that you might want to pick different values than those listed by default in the optimizer: you might want to optimize for a different purpose (such as a phase 3 Sith Triumvirate Raid team, where speed can be detrimental), you might want to choose something different to optimize against, or you might simply have a better set of values that you want to employ.
4.4: The easiest way to get started with the optimizer is to choose from the pre-programmed character templates. These are set up with sets of characters and targets that should fit various game modes. If there's no template to fit your exact needs, you can use one as a starting point or create one from scratch. For each individual character, if no target exists that matches what you want, you can select "Custom", or simply hit the "Edit" button to bring up the character edit modal.

5.Headline: Picking target values
5.1: Most characters will have the "basic" mode selected by default. In basic mode, you select a value for all stats that is between -100 and 100. These values are weights that are assigned to each stat to determine its impoact for that character. Setting two values as equal means that those stats are about equally important for that character. In basic mode, the optimizer will automatically adjust the weights to fit the range of values seen in-game for that stat. For example, giving speed and protection both a value of 100 means that 1 speed is about equivalent to 200 protection (since you find much more protection on mods than you do speed).
5.2: If you want more fine-tuned control over the stat values, you can switch to "advanced" mode. In advanced mode, the values given are the value for each point of the listed stat. In advanced mode, if speed and protection are both given a value of 100, then the tool will never select speed, because it can more easily give that character much more protection. I suggest sticking to basic mode until you have a strong sense for how the tool works.
